transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-01 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - ACME), Priya Desai (Platform Engineer - ACME), Martin Ruiz (Security - ACME)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment options. Main topics: VPC peering vs Private Endpoints, region constraints (EU/US residency), routing and egress controls, KMS/HSM integration, and pilot next steps.

Topics: networking, VPC peering, private endpoints, transit gateway, cross-account peering, region constraints, SOC2/KMS, perf concerns (latency/cost tradeoffs)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we should have about 50 minutes together. quick intro — i'm jordan, i'm the account exec for your account, and with me is sofia from our infra team.
[00:12] Sofia: hi! thanks, yeah happy to dig in on networking details — we've run these setups a bunch.
[00:18] Liam: yeah thanks. i'm liam, i'll kick us off — short background, we're evaluating Redwood because we need an on-prem-ish private deployment for our inference workloads, lots of PII and industrial control data. main ask is private connectivity to our AWS accounts in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[00:34] Priya: and we have a transit gateway already between our prod VPCs, we can share peering info.
[00:39] Martin: from security i'm mostly concerned about data at rest, KMS integration, audit logs and where egress leaves the VPC.
[00:46] Jordan: great, that's helpful. can you share your top requirement — is it full isolation (no internet egress) or just private endpoints + strict routing?
[00:56] Liam: ideally minimal internet egress. we'd prefer private endpoints into our VPCs and all traffic stays in region. but we also want the option to run a dedicated Redwood deployment in our VPC or connect to Redwood Private in our VPC, not sure of the terminology.
[01:12] Sofia: right — we offer Redwood Private which can be deployed in a customer VPC or we can run a customer-dedicated control plane with private endpoints. two patterns: 1) customer-hosted nodes inside their VPC (full private), 2) Redwood-hosted Private with VPC peering or private link. both are possible, tradeoffs are around operational surface and latency.
[01:31] Martin: what's the difference with peering vs private endpoints? we use aws privatelink a lot internally.
[01:38] Sofia: peering is usually direct VPC-to-VPC routing, simpler for L3 traffic and lower cost depending on egress. privatelink (interface endpoints) is more controlled and uses ENIs, often easier for cross-account restrictions but can add per-GB charges. also peering doesn't support transitive routing, so if you use a transit gateway that's a consideration.
[01:58] Priya: we do use a transit gateway, so we'd prefer a pattern that works with TGW — any gotchas?
[02:04] Sofia: TGW is fine; you can attach the Redwood VPC to your TGW or do a peering attach on the agent VPC. caveat: if Redwood nodes are in a different account, need route table entries and sometimes proxying for private link. we (Sofia) continue: sometimes customers put the inference nodes in a shared infra account and use route table controls for prod access.
[02:25] Liam: latency — our control loop requires <80ms p99 for some models. will we see cross-region effect if the control plane is in us-east and nodes in eu-west?
[02:34] Sofia: yes cross-region introduces RTT. best practice is to colocate model serving in the same region as the VPC. control plane calls (telemetry/rollouts) can be proxied over private link or staged to a regional control plane; we support regional private control plane deployments but that may add cost.
[02:53] Jordan: given that, sounds like you want nodes in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and private connectivity in each region. is that fair?
[03:01] Liam: yep. also question — does Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys for model data?
[03:07] Sofia: yes, we integrate with KMS for encrypting model artifacts and runtime secrets; customers can bring keys (CMKs) and we support usage patterns for AWS KMS and HSM-like integrations. note: for private deployments on-prem we have an additional step for HSM connector.
[03:23] Martin: audit logs — can we ship CloudTrail-style logs to our S3 and retain for 7 years?
[03:29] Jordan: we provide audit logs and can stream to customer S3 buckets or to a SIEM via Kinesis; retention policies are on the customer side. we'll share the logging architecture doc.
[03:39] Liam: ok good. another constraint — regulatory: some workloads must remain in eu-west-1 only. can we ensure models and cache don't leave region?
[03:48] Sofia: yes you can pin model versions and serving pools to regions; KV cache is local to the serving nodes unless you explicitly enable cross-region cache replication. by default we'd keep KV cache local.
[04:02] Priya: thanks, that helps. on networking specifics, can you walk through the VPC peering steps and required inbound/outbound ports?
[04:09] Sofia: sure — high level: need to exchange VPC CIDRs, agree on route table updates, open certain ports on security groups for the inference traffic (TCP 443 for control plane, gRPC ports for model traffic — we sometimes use 1919 or 7000+, depends on config), and ensure NACLs allow ephemeral ports. for privatelink we create interface endpoints in your account and you allow the service ENIs. I'll send a template.
[04:37] Martin: are there any IPs we need to whitelist or cert bundles? we run strict egress rules.
[04:42] Sofia: for peering you don't need public IPs. for Redwood-hosted private endpoints we provide a list of internal service IPs per region for the ENIs. cert-wise we use mTLS between nodes and control plane; you can upload trusted CA or use our public-facing certs if your CA trusts them.
[05:00] Liam: pricing? does dedicated in our VPC cost more than Redwood-managed dedicated?
[05:05] Jordan: cost varies; customer-hosted nodes shift infra cost to you (EC2/GPU costs), Redwood charges a software/ops fee for the Private subscription. Redwood-hosted Dedicated has a committed monthly fee plus per-token pricing variations. i'll follow up with a sizing/pricing sheet.
[05:19] Priya: are there restrictions on GPU types? we run A10Gs and some A100 spot pools.
[05:25] Sofia: we support common Nvidia families, and can provide AMIs optimized for particular GPUs; for spot pools we recommend a tolerance configuration. for tight latency SLAs you may want reserved instances.
[05:36] Liam: for the pilot we'd probably spin up a small cluster in each region, say 2x A10g for dev and 4x A100 for staging. can you support mixed fleet?
[05:44] Sofia: yes mixed fleet supported, but be mindful of model compilation/quantization differences — we recommend pinning model variants per GPU class.
[05:53] Martin: security question: SSO / SAML integration into our corporate IDP — do you support SCIM provisioning and role-based access?
[06:00] Jordan: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, RBAC — we'll provide the admin docs and a checklist for entitlements.
[06:09] Priya: one more networking nit: egress to external package repos for model downloads — can we cache artifacts locally? we have no internet in our production VPCs.
[06:17] Sofia: we have an artifact caching option — you can pre-seed model artifacts into your internal S3/ART repo and we point the runtime there. if no internet we recommend pre-seeding and using S3 endpoints.
[06:29] Liam: perfect.
[06:31] [small crosstalk] Priya: (laughs) oh i forgot — what about version rollouts and canary traffic routing when nodes are private?
[06:38] Sofia: rollouts are controlled by the control plane; with private deployments the control plane can be regional or on-prem and uses the same rollout primitives. we support canary percentages and automatic rollback on error thresholds. that traffic shaping happens at the router layer inside the VPC.
[06:52] Martin: do you have SOC2 and pen test reports we can share with InfoSec?
[06:56] Jordan: yes — i'll attach the SOC 2 summary and the pen test redacted report. for Private deployments we also provide a deployment-specific security checklist.
[07:05] Liam: timeline — we'd like to run a 4-week pilot for a core model, starting mid-April if possible. is that feasible?
[07:12] Jordan: timeline looks doable — first step is to share CIDRs and decide whether you want customer-hosted nodes or Redwood-hosted Private with privatelink. after that we size and schedule the pilot.
[07:21] Priya: i'll gather CIDR ranges and region preferences, and get back by next week.
[07:26] Jordan: great. Sofia, any technical risks to flag?
[07:29] Sofia: only real risk is misconfigured routing with the TGW and overlapping CIDRs. also watch out for cross-account ENI limits if you go privatelink. otherwise we've run similar setups.
[07:42] [00:07:42 — transcript continues with Q/A and clarifications — timestamps every ~30-60s]
[07:42] Liam: can you also run a quick network benchmark once we get peering in place? latency/p99 and throughput?
[07:47] Sofia: yes we can run a sample perf test — we typically run a 2-hour load test with synthetic prompt traffic and measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. we'll need an endpoint to target.
[07:58] Priya: note — we have strict egress monitoring, some flows require ticketing for new peering. how long do peering setups usually take from your experience?
[08:06] Jordan: it depends on internal change control — once CIDRs and route updates are approved, typically 1-3 days for setup plus testing. approvals can add time.
[08:15] Martin: also please indicate any default logs we forward to our SIEM — we need format and fields.
[08:20] Jordan: will include log schema and sample events.
[08:24] Sofia: and for metrics — we expose per-route latency and token breakdown in the console; we can stream metrics to CloudWatch or Prometheus exporters as well.
[08:36] Liam: ok wrapping up — quick recap of next steps?
[08:40] Jordan: recap: 1) Jordan sends VPC peering checklist, SOC2 docs, pricing sheet. 2) Sofia schedules deep-dive next week for routing/privatelink details. 3) ACME sends CIDRs and preferred regions by 2027-04-08. 4) Redwood runs perf test after peering.
[08:57] Priya: thanks all.
[08:59] Martin: thanks.
[09:01] Jordan: bye everyone.

End of transcript.
